newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ SPORT, RUGBY UNION- Fullback Cullen still on the mend.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT, RUGBY UNION- Fullback Cullen still on the mend.

text.p: PALMERSTON NORTH, Jan 13 - Manawatu and All Blacks fullback Christian Cullen is still coming to full fitness after having cartilage removed from his injured knee at Auckland before Christmas, NZPA reported on Monday.
Cullen was able to do most of the fitness and strength exercises during the Hurricanes Super 12 team camp in Palmerston North over the weekend, except running.
Cullen, who had a much-needed break at the Coromandel area over the holidays, said he expected to be back running in the next two to three weeks.
That probably won't be early enough for the Hurricanes' practice match against their stand-by players and others at Gisborne on January 28.
The knee operation means Cullen will have bone rubbing against bone, which he said "is a bit of a bummer" but something he and many other sportsmen have to accept.
The Hurricanes' management was happy with the players' progress. Most recorded personal bests and were already ahead of where they were at the same time last year.
Coach Frank Oliver said it proved players had never been at their maximum fitness in the past.
"The concentrated training regimes show they have never been playing to their potential. Backs, for instance, haven't done weight training in the past."
Hurricanes' strength adviser Graeme Sciascia said they would need to be better conditioned because every other team would have improved too.
